solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Queen, during duty, to perform physical activity

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of another, so the queen goes inside the duty

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax charged on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A royal squeezes some exercise into her busy round of official engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' reads as obligation, but it is a tax on goods; 'during' sets Elizabeth Regina's initials within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out or train is to take physical exertion, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Charm, in French, church worker perhaps

parts.note: en is French for in
a worker ant is one kind of ant, so worker suggests the insect

explanation.surface: A French-speaking church volunteer has a charming manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to delight or bewitch them, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Sea duck behind heard at regular intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals says to take every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A duck is heard calling repeatedly from somewhere behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its soft down.

clue.text: Rosaceous shrub person from Dundee beheaded on holiday

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, or first letter, is cut off

parts.note: Dundee is a Scottish city, so a person from there is a Scot
Easter is a public holiday period

explanation.surface: A Dundonian loses his head over a plant while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' cuts SCOT to COT; ON is given as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a shrub of the rose family, Rosaceae, so it is a rosaceous plant.

clue.text: Wily little long-nosed animal digging primarily

parts.note: a shrew is a small mammal with a long pointed snout

indicators.note: primarily, meaning first of all, takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cunning small creature is busy burrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and wily both describe someone sharp and cunning in their judgement.

clue.text: Some yobbos looted European capital

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rioting louts plundered a city somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway's seat of government is in this city, making it a European capital.

clue.text: Maybe town crier disturbed others around university

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters wrap round the university letter
disturbed means upset or thrown into disorder, so the letters of others are rearranged

explanation.surface: A town crier has upset people living near the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' scrambles OTHERS into SHOTER, and 'around' places U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier makes public announcements at the top of his voice, an example of someone who yells.

clue.text: Elderly person outside taken away from soldier

indicators.note: the outside letters, first and last, are removed from the following word

explanation.surface: A veteran is someone who has been away from the army for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, an old person is called an oldie.

clue.text: Trainee accountant Edward recalled

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, signals the name being written backwards

parts.note: Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: An accountant in training called Edward is summoned back to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reads as called back, but here it means written backwards; Edward's pet form is the usual Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police, so a trainee.

clue.text: Suspect ponders answer

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A suspect under questioning takes time to think before replying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like the person in the dock, but it is the anagram signal on PONDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply to a question is to give a response, the verb sense of answer.

clue.text: Old playwright is visibly nervous with fruit knife, at the back

parts.note: someone who shakes is trembling with nerves
a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: at the back picks the final letter of the word knife

explanation.surface: A nervous actor waves a fruit knife about behind the scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare is the Elizabethan dramatist, the best-known writer of plays in English.

clue.text: First-rate Republican to be broadcast

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: An excellent Republican politician is about to appear on television.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) becomes AI, the figure 1 doubling as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that airs is transmitted on radio or television.

clue.text: Modern fortification somewhere in Northeast England

parts.note: new means modern or recent
a castle is a fortified building

explanation.surface: A newly built fort stands at a location in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a major city in the north-east of England, an example of such a place.

clue.text: Strand of yarn spoiled red hat

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined or damaged, so the letters of the words red hat are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A loose piece of wool has ruined a red knitted cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A single fine length of spun fibre used in sewing or weaving is a strand of yarn.

clue.text: Reportedly cycled with Pam, going over navigational aid

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to have cycled is to have rode a bike, the past tense rode

indicators.note: going over suggests turning over, so the name Pam is written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone says they went cycling with Pam, studying the route as they went.
explanation.walkthrough: RODE (cycled) is said aloud as ROAD; 'going over' turns PAM into MAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A road map is a plan of routes used for finding the way when travelling.

clue.text: Weapon found in British river — good grief!

indicators.note: found in says the weapon is located within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to discover a weapon lying in a British river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' places the weapon within the river's name; the Dee is a favourite crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of dismay or surprise, interchangeable in speech.

clue.text: European nursed indisposed customer possibly

indicators.note: indisposed means unwell, so the letters of nursed are out of order

explanation.surface: A European looked after a sick shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indisposed' looks like describing the customer, but it signals that the letters of 'nursed' are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: The final consumer of a product, such as a buyer, is the person who actually uses it.

clue.text: Damage line, dropping latest oceanic fish

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: dropping latest says the final letter of the word line is lost

explanation.surface: An angler damages his line and loses the deep-sea fish he hooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The marlin is a large game fish of the open ocean, with a spear-like snout.

clue.text: Awfully petty war absorbs a lawman in American West

indicators.note: absorbs means takes in, so the jumbled letters take the A inside them
awfully means dreadfully or badly, so the letters of petty war are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A dreadful little feud draws in a sheriff on the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges PETTY WAR, and 'absorbs' puts A inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was a famous deputy marshal of the Old West, known for the gunfight at the OK Corral.

clue.text: Extreme anger starts to worry receptionist at hospital

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the two following words

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Fury begins to trouble a hospital receptionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is intense rage, an old word for fury.

clue.text: Poor book promotion

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, promotes a product

explanation.surface: A book has had a weak marketing campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor quality work is substandard, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Constructed raised bath to contain the Italian

indicators.note: to contain says the reversed bath holds the next piece inside it
in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a tub is a bath
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A builder lifted up a bath to fit the Italian fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read from the bottom up; 'to contain' then wraps the result around the Italian article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built has been put together or erected, a synonym of constructed.

clue.text: Mostly respect a large naval commander

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to admire someone is to respect them
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Sailors largely hold their fleet commander in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' means the synonym for respect loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior officer commanding a fleet in a navy.

clue.text: An unmarried female, not suitable

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, shortened to a
Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A single woman is judged an unsuitable match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or out of place is amiss, as in 'something is amiss'.

clue.text: Shop distributed an element of beer

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of Shop are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A shop hands out one of the ingredients of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried flowers of the hop plant give beer its bitterness, so they are one of its ingredients.

clue.text: Financial supporter wearing singlet and gold

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'
a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, a singlet
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A wealthy backer turns up in a vest and gold jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts money into a business to back it is a financial backer.
